summary: Created a 3-phase, 1.25-hour plan for the narrowed arrow-notation reconciliation. Phase 1 moves 7 declaration lines (4 arrow to infixr:25, 3 iff to infixr:20) across the four in-scope files as one atomic batch; Phase 2 syncs the 2 LTL/Temporal docstring precedence tables; Phase 3 verifies via the 372-module targeted build recipe plus rfl capability checks. No call-site-fixing phases: research empirically proved transitive parse impact is zero. Propositional/Defs.lean and the HasImp rebind remain out of scope.
decisions_made: Edit set is 7 declaration lines, not 4: the co-declared iff at infix:30 in Modal/LTL/Temporal must move to infixr:20 alongside the arrow, or the arrow-only change leaves iff binding tighter (research confirmed by rfl).
No call-site remediation phases: research built all 372 modules in the dependency cone green under both the arrow-only and arrow+iff variants, so the set of sites needing fixes is empty.
Phase 1 declared Commit Mode atomic-batch so the arrow-only intermediate state -- which is exactly the known-inverted-iff hazard -- is never a commit boundary.

Phase 3 verification uses the targeted `lake build $(cat /tmp/targets.txt)` recipe only; a bare full lake build is forbidden because it stalls indefinitely on Propositional/Tableau/Intuitionistic/Scheme.lean.
Warning count 32 is treated as a hard gate, not an observation: a rise blocks phase closure.
Bimodal gets no iff edit (declares none) and Modal gets no docstring edit (has no header precedence table).
dead_ends: Do not re-investigate the infix:29 equivalence operator at Foundations/Logic/LogicalEquivalence.lean:33: real hazard in a minimal model, but every equivalence/arrow co-occurrence in the four subtrees is a comment.
Do not re-check turnstile notations: they use unannotated notation:50 arguments and are precedence-immune.
Do not re-check validity notations with annotated :50 arguments: they already require parentheses today, so nothing changes.

Do not move the conjunction (36) or disjunction (35) notations: order is preserved at either arrow precedence and both already require parenthesized arrow arguments; these belong to the notation-wide reconciliation.
Do not re-derive scope: Propositional/Defs.lean is owned by a sibling task with a standing-approval chain, and the HasImp rebind belongs to a different sibling task.
